title: Latency regression after model version rollout (rw-llama-70b-instruct v3.1 -> v3.2) impacting Chat completions
text:
Latency regression after model version rollout (rw-llama-70b-instruct v3.1 -> v3.2) impacting Chat completions

description:
Customer reported a sudden increase in end-to-end latency for chat completions after a model version rollout on rw-llama-70b-instruct. Regression correlated strongly with Redwood’s staged rollout from v3.1 to v3.2 in us-east.

Issue summary
- Symptom: p95 and p99 latency increased (customer observed and Redwood dashboards confirmed). Throughput stable; error rate unchanged.
- Trigger: model version rollout (v3.1 -> v3.2) started ~2025-11-18 16:05 UTC in us-east.
- Impact: degraded UX (timeouts on customer side at 12s client timeout); no material increase in 5xx.
- Scope: us-east primarily; eu-west unaffected (rollout not started there at the time).

Customer impact
- Asteria Search production workload (chat) saw p95 increase from ~1.9s to ~3.3s for comparable prompt sizes; p99 exceeded 8s.
- Customer mitigated temporarily by reducing max_output_tokens from 512 to 256 and increasing client timeout.

Environment / request profile
- Endpoint: /v1/chat.completions (streaming=false)
- Model: rw-llama-70b-instruct
- Parameters: temperature=0.2; max_output_tokens=512; typical prompt length 1.2k–1.8k tokens.
- Region: us-east

What we checked (high-level)
- API gateway: no saturation, no elevated queue time.
- Router: no fallback spikes, stable routing policy; capacity healthy.
- Serving runtime: per-token decode time roughly flat; prefill time increased.

Timeline (UTC)
- 2025-11-18 16:05: rollout begins (canary 5% traffic -> v3.2)
- 2025-11-18 16:22: perf-canary alerts: rw-llama-70b-instruct p95 latency +55% vs baseline
- 2025-11-18 16:40: customer report via Support; internal incident opened: INC-2025-11-18-042
- 2025-11-18 17:10: rollback decision for us-east (pin back to v3.1)
- 2025-11-18 17:28: rollback completed; latency returns to baseline within ~10 minutes
- 2025-11-19 01:15: root cause narrowed to runtime build flag/regression affecting prefill kernel selection for this model artifact
- 2025-11-19 03:40: hotfix PR opened to revert the change; v3.2.1 candidate built
- 2025-11-19 18:20: v3.2.1 canary in us-east passes; rollout resumes with guardrails

Canary + signals
- perf-canary scenario: ChatCompletion, 1500 prompt tokens, 256 output tokens
- Alert: p95 latency regression >30% (threshold) for 2 consecutive windows
- Supporting metric: runtime_prefill_ms increased; runtime_decode_ms stable; gpu_utilization stable

Investigation notes
- Correlation was tight with rollout gates (step function at the same timestamp).
- No evidence of capacity shortage (no queuing, no elevated batch sizes, no OOM spikes).
- Router fallback_reason distribution unchanged (no health/capacity/policy changes).
- Suspected model artifact change interacted with a runtime optimization toggle, selecting a slower prefill path for certain sequence-length distributions.

Mitigation / workaround
- Immediate: rollback model version in us-east to v3.1 (customer impact reduced quickly).
- Customer-side workaround: reduce max_output_tokens and increase timeout (not ideal; provided as temporary guidance).

Resolution
- Serving Runtime shipped v3.2.1 hotfix (reverting prefill kernel selection change) and re-ran canary.
- Rollout resumed with additional canary checks (prefill_ms guardrail) and slower ramp.

Taxonomy notes (for Reliability Program)
- Proposed incident_type: Latency regression
- Proposed subtype: Rollout regression (model version rollout / release-induced)
- Primary owner: Serving Runtime
- Secondary/consulted: Platform Control Plane / Smart Routing (for rollout controls + pin/rollback), SRE (incident process)
- Rationale: customer-facing latency regression caused by a model version release and runtime behavior; mitigation required rollback/hotfix rather than capacity actions.

Next steps / follow-ups
- Add explicit canary gate for runtime_prefill_ms deltas by model family.
- Add an incident-bot suggestion heuristic: if perf-canary regression aligns with model rollout start time, suggest subtype = rollout_regression.
- Document customer comms template for rollbacks vs long-running mitigations.

Customer communication
- Shared summary: identified regression introduced in latest model version in us-east; rolled back; preparing hotfix; will notify before re-rollout.
- Avoided over-specific root cause language pending full postmortem.

References
- Slack: #incidents (INC-2025-11-18-042), #support escalation thread
- Dashboard: Ops > Model performance > rw-llama-70b-instruct (us-east)
- PRs: redwood#28392 (hotfix), perf-canary#499 (additional guardrail test)
